title: Prospective cohort study on quantitative MR evaluation during extension of heart failure therapy for patients with univentricular heart or after atrial swith operation with d-transposition of the great arteries
summary: Patients with congenital heart defects who do not have a normal left ventricle as the systemic ventricle often suffer from heart failure over the course of their lives. Monitoring the success of heart failure therapy in this patient group is challenging, as both ultrasound examination of the heart and biochemical blood parameters provide insufficient information for this complex group. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a time-consuming but very precise functional examination of the heart in these patients with an atypical systemic ventricle. This study aims to evaluate the expansion of heart failure therapy with modern medications such as Sacubitril-Valsartan (Entresto®) or Empagliflozin (Jardiance®) using cardiac MRI in this specific patient group. The MRI results will be compared with the results from echocardiography and biochemical blood tests.

interventions.name: 20 patients each with Fontan circulation or atrial switch operation for d-TGA who are clinically stable but have experienced a worsening of the clinical situation within the last 6 months

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with Fontan circulation or atrial switch operation for d-TGA who are clinically stable but have experienced a worsening of their clinical condit ion within the last 6 months, necessitating an expansion of anti-congestive therapy from a clinical perspective. They should be in functional class 2 or 3 and, preferably, have shown an elevated end-diastolic pressure in the systemic ventricle during a cardiac catheterization within the last 24 months and/or a shift to a higher functional class
Exclusion criteria:
Excluded are patients in functional class 4 and patients with relevant pulmonary vascular pathology (transpulmonary gradient in Fontan patients ≥ 4 mm Hg). Also excluded are all patients whose concomitant medication cannot be kept constant during the 6-week observation period. Additionally, patients with type I diabetes mellitus, patients under 18 years of age, as well as patients with atrial fibrillation and end-stage renal failure (eGFR < 30 ml/min/1.73 m²) will not be included
